audit: Only four associations look both novel and statistically robust (PIK3R1 in pilocytic astrocytoma, 30/168 vs 9/1545; ARID1B in 'Rhabdomyosarcoma, NOS', 16/66 vs 7/1647; ZMYM3 in malignant glioma, 20/166 non-hypermutated vs 8/1547; ASXL1 in medulloblastoma, 17/212 vs 7/1501). I could not find ten novel findings, and I am not padding the list: every other candidate below the strong tier (e.g. CYP4F8, ANO9, DDX43, NOS3, LEPR, VAV1, FCGBP, SBF2) rests on 2-5 cases, does not survive multiple-testing correction across ~200,000 diagnosis-gene tests, and involves long or passenger-prone genes. I would not put them in a paper. Caveats on the novel four: their variants are almost all scattered, unique missense changes with no hotspots or domain clustering, which is unusual for true drivers (canonical PIK3R1 drivers are iSH2 in-frame indels), so they need orthogonal validation (independent cohort, germline review, functional work) before being headlined. ARID1B is concentrated in the NOS rhabdomyosarcoma label but largely absent from the embryonal/alveolar subtypes, which is biologically odd and could reflect a sub-cohort or pipeline batch. Cohort issues: 18 hypermutated tumors (>200 mutations, up to 15,731; mostly malignant gliomas, likely MMR/POLE) were excluded from testing because they make every gene look enriched. Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlapping (ICD-O terms such as 'Neoplasm, malignant', 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Glioma, malignant' vs 'Glioblastoma' vs 'Astrocytoma, NOS'; 'Craniopharyngioma' vs adamantinomatous), so the comparison groups contain the same tumor biology under other labels, which dilutes contrasts. 124 cases have no non-synonymous mutation at all, consistent with low pediatric burden but also with fusion/copy-number drivers (BRAF-KIAA1549, PAX-FOXO1, SMARCB1 deletions) that this data type cannot see, so expected frequencies for those entities are underestimates. Recurrent identical variants across unrelated diagnoses (e.g. C17orf80 p.S281R in 5 cases, ABCF1 p.P9L in 10) suggest residual germline or artifact calls. BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E (alternate transcript). Many subtypes have fewer than 10 cases, so frequency estimates for them are imprecise.
methods: Built a case-by-gene binary matrix of non-synonymous somatic mutations from mutations.csv joined to cases.csv. Excluded 18 hypermutated cases (>200 mutations) and kept them out of the background. For each diagnosis label and each gene mutated in at least 3 cases, ran a one-sided Fisher exact (hypergeometric) test of that diagnosis vs all other cases, with Bonferroni/BH-style correction over all diagnosis x gene pairs (~2e5 tests). Inspected top hits for variant class, hotspot structure, mutation burden, co-mutation and demographic clustering, then assigned replication probabilities from statistical strength, case counts and prior biological knowledge. Expected frequencies are shrunk observed rates in non-hypermutated cases.
